title: Odd-n limit ρ→∏(1−2^{-i}) is left as a conjecture (problem not solved for odd n)

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body: The problem asks to DETERMINE $\rho(n)$ and its asymptotics. For odd $n$, Theorem `thm:asy`(2) and Remark `rem:oddlimit` state the limit $\prod_{i\ge1}(1-2^{-i})=0.288788\ldots$ but call it a conjecture: "Proving this is the genuinely hard analytic core ... We leave this as a conjecture." The supporting heuristic ("if the rows were iid uniform") is acknowledged invalid: the rows of $E_S$ are Reed-Muller evaluation vectors satisfying RM dual relations, hence strongly dependent. No rigorous argument shows this dependence does not change the limiting singularity probability of the square $\tfrac N2\times\tfrac N2$ matrix $E_S$. Numerics ($\rho(5)\approx0.32,\ \rho(7)\approx0.16$) are non-monotone, far from the limit at small $n$. Suggested route: use generating identity `eq:genid` $\mathbb E_R[2^{M-\mathrm{rank}\,E_R}]=\sum_g 2^{-\mathrm{wt}(g)}$, derive an analogous first/second-moment identity for balanced $S$ and bound the variance to localize $\Pr[\mathrm{rank}\,E_S=M]$; or a coupling showing low-weight RM dual relations are asymptotically negligible. Until proved, the odd case is unsolved.
